advice: There is no advice I can give. The big people are always going to be more important than the little people (who makes the CEO a lot of money). And people will continue to quit and you will always be hiring
pros: The pay is kinda decent
cons: Where to start? Never work here!! Santander hires everyone who applies. They don't drug test which they should because about 80% or more of the employees smoke weed. I even know some employees who snort cocaine. It's awful!! I have never worked for such an unprofessional company. Managers are not qualified. They promote people they like not who is right for the job. I worked there for 6 months before I got training and a manager. I'm not just a bitter employee and in fact I never leave reviews for my previous jobs. Just please trust me when I say Do Not Work Here!!

advice: Instead of writing your employees up, maybe give them the tools so that they can be successful at their jobs. If you can’t do that, at least be more understanding and patient when such large changes take place. There is always an adjustment period that people may need a little help with.
pros: I worked there for about 8 years and we were like family. I enjoyed working there and got to know the customers well.
cons: A new manager came on and we didn’t really get along, he wrote me up for stuff that was beyond my control and when I asked for help because I was being buried with the extra workload they dumped on us after the switch, I was denied.

advice: Managers that have issues working with people, should not work in banking. Rising above popularity contests or personal grievances would make a good leader. Anything less is a waste of not only company time and money, but also those striving to better themselves or keep food on their families table. A person should only be let go if they are not performing the said job, not because they are not popular.
pros: Company culture was great! The company definitely set incentives to create a comfortable learning atmosphere for most employees.
cons: Management was not supportive when it came to bullying from other or from management itself. Human resources didnt provide any protection for lower level employees, especially part-time floaters, from management not managing correctly.

advice: Since they do not take or solicit advise, I have none to give other than gut the place and find new management
pros: Work life balance is pretty good.  Pay is decent.  Bonus can be expected.  Most people try as hard as they can and to the best of their abilities.
cons: Inefficient senior management, too many office politics, no sense of direction, unreasonable workloads.  Stupidity is commonplace, expected, and rewarded.  ER does nothing to help any employee regardless of section of the bank,  Business Partners are constant cogs in the wheel, talent management is almost non-exsistent, recruiting is useless, learning and development can't get it together, and I would like to know what compensation does.  The only good group seems to be Payroll.

summary: Good place to start, because the wage is above average. if you are responsible of tasks, the wage is not proportional
advice: Management is really concern in reaching the objective. Personal situation seldom count. Anyway this is slowly getting better and started to improve recently
pros: Banco Santander is a good place to start working. Very good start salary, benefit to take a loan, services near working place (nursery, hospital, shops). Bank has a very wide range of activities and business and the opportunity to learn are very high, also if you have some experience or ideas you can add your point.
cons: Very long working day (even if now is improving). No extra hours paied. Very hierarchical organization, needed contacts to improve and change department. Your opinions generally are not listened and you have to fight to be listen, or accept the situation as is.

advice: Branch management is fine. Corporate management needs to clarify objectives and update procedure and support upgrading outdated and unstable banking software.
pros: I enjoy the people I work with on an every day basis. The branch staff in the district make it feel very much like belonging to a club.
cons: Poorly organized and unhelpful departments, every inter-departmental communication feels like a battle. Management has no clear direction. Policies are outdate and nearly impossible to decode yet everyone will expect you to be an expert and have memorized the policy database. Often a call to the support desk ends up with unknowledgeable employees reading obtusely written policy PDFs or just referring the policy number before just hanging up. No advancement, positions filled internally by pre-decision. Slow and unstable banking software that has employees sometimes unable to complete basic transactions

summary: Good Part-time job if you are not seeking advancement (retirees)
advice: Take a course on personnel management and human resources.  The worst thing a new manager can do is come in to a new environment and try to change everything to his/her liking, whether it is Santander way or not.    A course would educate management on how to speak to personnel so as not to alienate them and to perform as a team.  No one performs well under pressure or bullying.
pros: Great customer relations if you build them; 401K matching, most staff are a pleasure to work with, good comradery among tellers and platform personnel.
cons: Always short staffed, many new managers have not a clue as to how to manage personnel or the workings of the system, including operations and banking systems with Santander.

advice: Stop being so uptight ... Don't promise more knowing your not going to come through. Give recognition where it is do
pros: Salary is great for what I'm used to. The company is laid back and causal dress. Hour lunches and a lot of food places close by. Been there 7 months now and so far so good. Plenty of opportunities and also was hired with no experience.
cons: Avps micro manage and lied about promotions and raises. Because it's a call center it's a lot of drama and mess and I've went to high school with a lot of people there so it's always he say , she say when I blink. A lot of sexual scheming to get to where people want to be .... Seems the only way to get to where you wanna go , I'd rather work hard for it !

jobTitle: CARD PORTFOLIO CONTROL TEAM - PROJECT MANAGER II
summary: CARD PORTFOLIO CONTROL TEAM - PROJECT MANAGER II
pros: Implementing new Credit Cards products, testing and validating for any work stream impact, working with different teams internal and external vendors within the Operation Unit by solving pending and open systems issues. Creating new workflows operational and accounting procedures to control and prevent any losses and completing projects in a timely matter to support group organizational goals and make recommendations. Responsible to validate GLs balances for Quality Controls by reporting Losses and Write off Accounts for Disputes and Collections cases.
cons: Preparing, analyzing and developing strategies to improve financial control operation models and build supports to maintain business structures to validate daily accounting activity. Implementing strategies to prevent and improve deliverables to support new and efficient work strategies to reduce operations risk. Research and resolve open and pending issues with the technical support team and project managers.

summary: I have a good opinion about this company
advice: Improve this problem with the careers inside the company.
pros:
In general terms, if you deserve it you have good changes of being promoted an also there are opportunities for changing you career inside the company. 
Wok-life balance I would say is positive, of course you can work as many after hours as you like but also many people leaves work on time and that is no problem.
Benefits are very good. Excellent Health insurance, 401K among others
cons:
Salary is below average. 

In general the careers inside the company are not developed, I mean that there are employees with good experience and there may be a junior that just came to the company, and even may have no prior experience, and he/she can still have better salary than the older and experienced one. Simple does not make sense.

summary: Governance Risk and Compliance / GRC Unprecendented Horror
advice: Try providing a suggestion box for anonymous feedback. The /severe/ turnover rate is alarming even against Santander's standards. You need to listen to what is happening in GRC,  Who ever placed upper management over this group it makes your business judgement highly questionable.
pros: It provided a continual pay check until another position was found. Insurance. This position taught me to assess other jobs for more than salary and name prominence. People outside of the GRC department were good people to work with. Good benefits.
cons: GRC Management Bullying. Management has no idea what Governance Risk or Compliance is. Nor can it grow the organization. ***It's in the red to be cut if it cant hire a slew of bodies because turnover has remained so high***.  Moral is shameful. No opportunities for growth although there are a /plethora/ of empty seats in the group. Micromanagement that is stressful under a particular manager. Very unapproachable and repelled people as many of us gravitated away.

advice: Hire based on knowledge instead of your friends and relatives. Learn your teams job functions. Appreciate your employees. Communicate better.
pros: NRH location is close to my home. The pay is good  for some.
cons: Very hard to advance if you're not a part of a clique or related to someone. When someone gets promoted the first question asked is who is he/she related to. I've seen two AVP's get demoted to manager positions just because they weren't liked by upper management. HR is a joke. A few managers are great at their jobs but most are lazy and don't bother to learn the job functions of their employees. I make a good salary for what I do which is the only thing keeping me there. If I ever find a company that will pay what I make now I would quit without hesitation.

jobTitle: Licensed Relationship Banker- Small Business Specialist
summary: Great for business, hard for retail
advice: Bridge the gap to keep experienced retail employees in the company.  Many are highly skilled and want to advance.  They find it extremely challenging to do so.
pros: Many genuinely kind coworkers so people get along very well
cons: Retail:. Minimum wage for tellers on their first day is $17/hr but other rules haven't seen pay increases. Incentive pay decreased. With eight years experience in finance, licenses and commercial banking experience and top performer success, I'm making less than $5/hr more than the entry level starting wage. Retail is not considered as highly when applying out to risk and operations positions so moving internally is generally regarded as futile in retail even with years of experience and excellent internal recommendations. It's frustrating when YOY your total compensation is decreasing and you want to be loyal to the company.

advice: As long as management continues to listen to and are open to new ideas, it will stay far ahead of the competing banks in the area.
pros: I am a 20 + year banker who has worked for many banks in that time. I had heard good things about Santander so decided to post a resume' about a job I was interested in. The HR experience was excellent throughout the process leading up to the offer letter. I find the bank has a very good environment-treating employees well and open to new ideas Very happy so far.
cons: Technology could be better but it's not a deal breaker in my opinion.

summary: Financially rewarding, but not well treated (Mexico branch)
advice: too many!! of you to few of the actual employe. Take care of the costumer not just saying it
pros: they pay good money and the bonus are spectacular, they train their employees and they invest on them as well. they always pay what they offer it can take 15 more days but they always pay and in what money is related they are cristal clear.
cons: They treat their employees like machines and sometimes in a not very "human" way to may "generals" to few soldiers. They exploit the middle and low positions and they treat their costumer as if they were making them a favor.

advice: Try to be productive.
pros: Salary (as IT contract with US companies ....), location (BOSTON is beautiful), Good company for trainees or people with no more than 5 years of experience.
cons: As the Data Center is in Mexico and the support laboratory or developers is in Spain everything es very, very, extra, plus complicated and %100 bureaucratic, don't forget that the owner are Spanish people. They are overly concerned with procedure at the expense of efficiency or common sense. The managers change everything at any time without any reason and they make pressure to  employees to do these change  at last moment (usually after 6 pm...) . The meetings time are rarely less than 2 or 3 hours and 2 o 3 times every day. If you are a IT engineer with more than 5 years, be careful..

summary: Worst technology ever experienced in a company; they hamper your ability to do your job
advice: Change the 'boys club' environment that values 'pedigree' over actual skills and capabilities.  Get rid of the IT department and hire a new group of people whose skills aren't stuck in the 1990's.  Change the rigid promotion system that locks people in and prevents your best employees from rising to the top.
pros:
There are some great managers; it's very individualistic
Decent benefits
cons:
Worst IT department I have seen in my 25 years of working; never really had the tools to do my job
No vision at leadership level; everything is lip service
No focus, always looking at the next bright and shiny object
No concept of customer loyalty; when a place has no loyalty to its employees, that is the end result

summary: Very professional. A big  and impressive culture, always aiming to be the best.
pros: You're pushed to the next level. There is a great spirit in the teams and from day 1 I felt like being part of a family. It has been years since I worked there, but I still cherish those moments with great joy. I've been lucky to work with such highly skilled individuals. For me personally, I was most impressed by how the various branches across Europe were able to collaborate effectively, while dealing with so many languages. There were a ton of opportunities.
cons: Santander is very organized and structured. It takes a while to change things.

advice: Treat your employess like humans not a number. We make Tom Dundon a lot of money and while he's enjoying a luxury lifestyle the employees that are working the hardest don't get the recongnition that they deserve. STOP managing by fear!! Promote from within it's a GREAT moral booster.
pros: I do love what I do I just like how the company is ran. Getting a consistent paycheck
cons: This is the most ass backwards company that I ever worked for they don't value the quality employee and could care less if you had good skill set its all about how much butt you kiss to move up. We constantly hear about reps getting hired with NO experience.  They hardly promote from within and never give raises. They cut your pay then want you to work even harder for less money.

advice: My only advice is good luck keeping this company alive in the States because at this rate there's only going to be 5 employees left by 2016 in the US.
pros: I had decent coworkers at my branch but that was it.
cons: Stupidly high sales goals, care more about sales than customer service. Upper management hounds you for the tiniest things, there's zero communication and staffing is awful. Extremely high turnover rate and everyone I've ever know who's worked there or currently works there absolutely hates it. They can't keep employees because they're treated like garbage and it's so obvious within a month of being there how bad it really is because even customers hate the institution and complain about pointless fees. I would never, ever recommend this company to anyone as a customer or employee.

advice: At some point you need to trust that the employees have the best interests of the customer in mind and empower then with the tools and resources to do the job. Re-evaluate your compensation strategy that will allow you to put in place the best and brightest so that you can remove those that do not perform.
pros: I have a saying, "There is opportunity in chaos". Well, there is a lot of opportunity if you have the mental toughness and maturity to deal with change and ambiguity. Things have improved over the last 6 months no that they have a CEO who understands the American banking industry, but that is going to take some time for it to trickle down into the entire organization, especially to the customer facing support areas.
cons:
1) A lot of Ex-pats were brought on after the acquisition that did not understand American banking. That appears to be changing.
2) Whose bright idea was it anyway to go from a regional thrift to a national bank with what appears to be no consideration or analysis that the current structure could support it.? Was that decision made in Madrid? Not a very bright idea.  
3) Mid tier leadership is weak. There is not leadership development and as such there are people in mid tier roles that should not be there.
4) A lot of CYA/Just-in-case busy work that prevents real work from being done.
5) Antiquated infrastructure and technology along with no internal customer service culture or mentality. When there is not enough network bandwidth to support the everyday work, you have a major problem on your hands. That is not helped by an IT support desk that has lengthy SLAs.
6) Senior management says that they want people to be empowered, but that is just not the case. There is a lack of trust between management and the employees. That is not helped by a compensation strategy that does not attract the best and brightest.

advice: Actually use "The Ear," stop micromanaging, realize that people have lives outside of work, stop having your managers text employees after hours about work stuff.
pros:
Paid pto
Decent pay
You get overtime
cons:
If you have vacation plans already setup or if you wanna go somewhere in the future forget it. You have to book it the same month.
Don't rely on your incentive plan for pay it because it can change at any moment and dramatically impact the pay  
The system is entire computer terribly slow which ultimately impacts the customer experience. Customer experience impacts your pay. 
Management says things like they want to get you licensed, but it will never happen because they keep false promises.
I would never work here if I was a settled "grown-up" married with children because there is no  work-life balance.

advice: The problems I had had nothing to do with my immediate manager. He was a great manager. The problem was that not much was done, further up, to get a quick coverage when a someone leaves the job
pros: Great culture overall. My branch had a small team and we worked closely, supporting each other to bring our numbers up.
cons: Obviously...compensation and coverage was a big problem as well. Working part time in that role pays a miniscule amount and as the face of the operation, there was a lot of work to do, especially when working alone due lack of coverage.

summary: fast pace and then faster pace
advice: walk the walk - if people are being valued, reward your people, really listen and give them a fare share of what the company makes due to their hard work
pros: always on the  move in getting into new business, more growth, good for CEO and people have a stake in the company's prosperity - highlevel management and owners
cons: constantly is very demanding, more and more work but tactical solutions constantly because of time pressure time-to-market, thus causing shaking foundation

summary: A great place to work until it went public.
advice: If there are reasons why a territory is struggling, listen to your area sales managers. They are the face of the company and get feedback from dealers every day.
pros: Above average pay, flexibility for area sales managers, a lot of great people to work with, high tech for its industry.
cons: Greed at the top. Sales obstacles differ per territory, but upper management has no authority to make changes. Company motto: It is what it is.

advice: Should consider pay and benefits that is on par with the rest of the industry. Also other benefits such as work from home will add to quality of life and possibly retain staff.
pros:
- Benefit to speak spanish
- Small environment with exposure to most executives
- Bonus pay is average to above average
cons:
- Base Pay is well below average
- Health, Retirement, and Other Benefits are well below average
- A revolving door in many areas. If you are not Spanish will be difficult to succeed.

advice: I have no advice to management, thuoght the process was very well scheduled, and all of the details lined up as the process moved along which is not the case with a lot of internships.
pros: Beautiful office, great people, relevant work, great training, great location, great amentities, overall just a great experience for an intern.
cons: At times the work for intern was a bit light and could go a day or two without having a relevant assignment, but that is the world of interns, right?

advice: To have an open space where we all can learn the programs and system together instead of trying to communicate with all of the workers on a one on one basis I think we would all be on the same page if we were in training together.
pros: I loved working with all of my co-workers as well as my managers and I also loved learning the system and learning about the job.
cons: Is when I had to leave because my contract was up.

advice: the banking industry is transforming at a high pace, and building a culture of innovation requires a workplace where failure is allowed and seen as an opportunity to learn and get better. Santander culture is not really there yet.
pros:
Great place to grow
Stability 
Careers opportunities. In Spain you can move between companies within the holding
cons:
Santander is a multinational group, but don't expect to find opportunities to move between countries. They are very rare and not incentivaced. 

Diversity is a work in progress

advice: Every single thing you are doing now, do differently.  Listen to your employees and give them incentives to perform.
pros:
Decent but not stellar benefits package
Decent work - life balance
cons: The Spanish have no idea how to run a US company (and as it turns out they don't really know how to run a Spanish company either). They prefer to hire layer upon layer of incompetent management from the outside, rather than promote good people from within.  The bureaucracy there is as bad as it gets anywhere.  To say they have substandard information technology would be paying them a huge compliment. Management ranges from mediocre to completely incompetent.  The pay stinks.

summary: A very good company to work for.
advice: It is best for managers to remain professional and treat all employees the same.  Managers should not have lunch and social gatherings with one employee and leave others out.
pros: The company has great benefits.  The managers are understanding.  The job is fun.  The dress code is relaxed.
cons: In my experience, the managers play favorites.  It is hard to get a deserved promotion or raise.

advice: Spend some time in the middle market / average branches. Not only the top performing, and busy ones.
pros: Hourly pay is good based on experience.
cons: Commission and Bonus structure changed. The goals are much harder to reach, and commission is tied into bank side revenue. Unless you're in a very busy branch, a major city, or have a ton of connections, it's unlikely to receive a bonus worth the work required.

advice: Either commit to a strategy and fix this dump, or bite the bullet and sell to Wells Fargo.  Do yourself and 1,500 employees a solid favor.
pros: 401k match, parking lot, they require more words for pros...  So I'll say...  They made the stables where they packed people into like cord wood a pleasant color.
cons: Employees can't possibly adapt to the constant changes in leadership and strategic direction.  Health Insurance is the worst I've ever encountered.  Not a good place to work.  They should hand out Zoloft at the door on the way in.  People who work there really hate this place.

advice:
More training. Actual training. Not the same 4 SPPs every single day for time unending.
Simplify and consolidate portals. Update computers and networks. 
Actually find out what is happening in your branches. The CEO says work/life balance is important, but your DE basically makes it mandatory that you work 50hrs/week.
pros:
Met some wonderful branch level employees
Trainers are great people
Operates on a P&L system
Audits are very easy to pass
cons:
The computer systems are just a devastating mess. They are slow and antiquated. You have to go through a maze of 3 different portals just for the most basic of account services. Add to that the many different programs for lending and bankers, then the portals for teller and it's terrible. You can't have more than 3 windows open or your system will slow down and crash. It's terrible when you are in front of a customer and you have to small talk them to death just to deposit a check and see if there are any products you can offer them to make your sales goals. 
Mortgages and investments have to go through offsite partners that are terrible at calling customers or following up in any capacity. 
High level managers are mean and rude and show no concern at all for anything you have to raise to their level. We have to consult a District Executive just to make a suggestion to The Ear. We get grilled over sales goals, but they cut incentives. 
They allow bullying and mistreatment of employees to the point where people from other branches know it's happening, but no one will say anything because we are scared of losing our jobs over it. 
It takes a long time to learn the organization of the company and all the responsibilities of your position. You only get 10 days of training each for platform and teller. Not even close to enough time. They want you to learn at your branch, but everyone is so desperately understaffed that you get thrown to the wolves immediately.

summary: It's all about who you know!!!
advice:
To the managers in collections... Please treat others how you would want to be treated... Just because we are reps does not mean you can talk or treat us like we're children. We have lives outside of this job and coming to work everyday shouldn't be so hard. At one point you were sitting in the same seat! I understand there ARE people here that make it hard for you guys but I'm speaking for the people who come in and work! We really just need new managers. Our current managers are set in their ways. I don't see this EVER changing until the bad ones are out. Santander has lost touch with their people. I was there when the company was great and I miss it! 

To the AVP's there are well qualified people on the phones who want more out of their careers! Give people a chance!
pros:
The pay is GREAT!! No company can beat it! I've been here for 6yrs so I'm not sure what the starting rate is now, I have heard it's much less now. 

Casual Dress code... Jeans and if you have enough company shirts you can get away with wearing those throughout the week!
cons:
Management is horrible... If you do fall under a good manager don't get comfortable because that can change at anytime. Managers are completely disconnected. The treatment is not so good! It doesn't matter if you perform well or not! Things have changed since going public! 

The opportunity to move up within the company or change departments is not likely! It's all about WHO YOU KNOW! I have been here for 6 years and I perform well! Performing well does not matter! I've applied to so many positions and NOTHING. I was once told by management that when a position does open up they already have someone in mind or someone lined up for the position. So even if you get an interview if you don't have any connections you WILL NOT get the position. 

You are required to work a late night... why not create a shift that will work better for people and their families... There are people here that would rather work a later shift!

summary: A good company to work with!
advice: Maybe they should have  a wider spread of people in terms with who they recruit so that there is a diverse environment.
pros: A very good work environment and a good city to work in! Not a lot of opportunities but has a good reputation as a company.
cons: There are not any big downsides I can think of! The only thing would be a reason unrelated to the company and that would be me driving a lot to reach the company everyday morning!

summary: Terrible credit delivery, management and mediocre systems.
advice: Try to find qualified senior management who understand the business and the market so you can save what is left.
pros: Nothing i can think of.   Very low productivity staff and minimal competition internally which allow you to stand out easily.  Open door management, they listen but dont act.
cons: Terrible credit delivery and old school management.  hyper focus on calling activity and micro management but not paying attention about delivering for the customers.   They have a pessimistic view of their staff and do not trust or respect their bankers, even if you are a top producer.   Business banking is managed by retail folks who have no clue about the business.

advice: Management needs to be trained on how to be leaders, not just people in charge.
pros: Hated the place for a looong time (working in the "call center") but the corporate location is a whole different world. Many opportunities to move up in the company, much more professional atmosphere, and competitive wages.
cons: As stated above, the call center/collections/customer service positions and office were terrible. I dreaded going to work every day, managers were uninformed and unmotivated (and unmotivating), it was basically a sweat shop atmosphere.

advice: Wake up and take responsibility for what is going on. So much money spent but not where it should be. Update technology now.
pros: In branch team members are great.
cons:
The organization of this bank is out of control. Corporate preaches Respect, but you won’t get any as branch team members. Every district is run differently. DE’s just do what they want. So much negativity!
Employees are constantly told you’re not good enough. Unrealistic goals. Bankers have to fight for every penny of their incentive. Too many trackers and none match up. I’ve never seen a company where no one is accountable for their actions. P &L is a joke. The attrition rate is so high in branches but HR never tries to look into what is going on.

summary: Immature environment that promotes a lethargic culture
advice: Please stop cherry picking favorites for special projects and take the time to grow loyal employees
pros: Great individual contributors, good starting salary, secure job, good low level managers, nice bathrooms, good meeting rooms, good natural light in the office
cons: Lack of clear career advancement, every project must be done "yesterday", high level of secrecy among C-level to mid level managers, no communicated vision for department, HR department is disengaged on employee issues and slow to react to issue reporting

summary: This is a good short term place to work but I wouldn't recommend trying to build a career here long term.
advice: Consistency following company policy would help. Adequate heads up for mandatory overtime should be standard policy.
pros: The pay and the benefits are good. You get health insurance and PTO accrual from day one. There was a lot of room for growth in the Mesa call center. When I worked in collections the bonus structure was great in the year I spent in collections there was only 2 months I didn't get a bonus and my bonuses weren't under $600 but I think they have changed the bonus structure since I've left so this may be different now.
cons: My opinion is based on my experience working in the Mesa location from what other employees from the Denver and Texas locations have told me some of these issues are nonexistent there. This is a call center position so they will try to restrict your time off the phone I hope you don't have to go to the bathroom outside of your 2 15 minute breaks and your lunch because they will start writing you up. Whether or not any company policy was followed depends on the manager you speak to so if one manager says no if you keep asking you'll probably find one that will say yes. Their overtime policy could be good or bad depending on what your life outside of work is like but they do have mandatory overtime sometimes and they do not give you an adequate heads up. There has been more than one occasion where an AVP has sent an email at 3pm telling you there's mandatory overtime effective immediately so you have to stay after your scheduled shift time. Also since Arizona does not participate in daylight savings your schedule will shift an hour later from about November to March. So if you work 9-6 normally you will work 10-7 and your late night will go from 12-9 to 1-10 but you will get a 5% differential if you work past 9. This was my first call center so some of these issues may be typical.

summary: A trully international group where you can find well-prepared people among managers and collaborators
advice: The perception is that top management is too well paid compared to the rest. In the years of record profit figures there hasn't been a fair distribution of bonuses with the employees in the base.
pros: Trackrecord of innovation, a good place to learn, salaries above average in the sector, chances for an international carrier
cons: For the majority of employees who work at the branches (commercial bank) there is too much commercial pressure compared to their salaries

summary: Not a first tier regional bank - yet
advice: Flatten the structure. Hire more middle management and boots on the ground. Demand more from IT.  Bring more meritocracy to promotions and focus on developing leaders , not just talkers in the upper levels. Get rid of senior leaders who play politics but don’t produce results
pros:
Competitive base pay , good bonus structure particularly for more junior positions ; all cash bonus for most grades and typically people do get close to or at target levels in my experience. Good 401k match. 
There are plenty of smart and hard working colleagues as well. Work life balance is fairly good but with Covid flexibility is now the norm everywhere.
cons:
Fixing issues and resolving MRAs have been the focus for past few years and yet so much remains. Technology is terrible, a lot of money is spent but I struggle to see where it all goes. The list of manual error prone processes that should be automated or made more efficient with tech makes my head hurt.

People get burned out from spending all their time fixing problems only to find more - every time you look deep into a process you will likely find something broken.

Politics are everywhere in banking but this is by far worst I’ve seen. Lots of empire building and people attempting to justify salaries.  Much energy that could go into making the bank better wasted on internal squabbles and finger pointing.  

Getting promoted is more about back room dealing and being part of the inner circle than anything else. Roles often aren’t posted or if they are it is a token posting with a candidate already selected.  

Bottom line - heavy (and expensive)  management layer with sky high expectations and few doers to get in there and resolve problems and get stuff done. If you are a doer it’s a thankless task as you will get asked to do more with less each year.   

The new CEO (Tim) may be heading in right  direction but much work remains to compete with the better regional banks and improve the culture and reputation of the firm.

advice:
Review what other competitors are doing to keep their employees and do it!
For the love of God, change the compensation packages
Embrace work/life balance (work from home) - the culture here is mediocre compared to other banks
pros: At least i got a job....
cons:
-Work Life balance policy is implemented, but no one is allowed to use it. 
-You are limited to recruiting mediocrity because compensation is one of the worst in Wall Street
-Promote people to management positions with no training or development (not real managers)
-everything revolves around Boston office.

advice: Work as a team. Be transparent. Colleagues are much more likely to understand intentions if they are transparent and working together, rather than saying one thing to get the team behind an idea, but then doing something different.
pros:
Company benefits (cell discounts, product discounts, etc)
Looks good on a resume
Makes you feel important (titles, what responsibilities you are given)
Probably a place to improve if you know someone that knows someone, and are over the top with goals, and there are openings available (where other interviewees don't have these same plusses)
cons:
NOT transparent with cold calling and selling - does not keep traffic and customer base in mind when setting goals

Selling expectation evolved from awareness and what is good for the customer, to pushing products for goals and numbers - yes it's a business, but must we be so pushy and nosy? Why sit down with a customer who wants to open a checking account, and ask every question known to man to get them to buy as many products as we can recommend. Why not start with what the customer needs and came in for, and grow with the customer as conversation and relationship grows with the bank?

Hours have changed from "banker's hours" which were highly sought after, to call nights after hours, later and later into the evening, and even talk of additional call nights if numbers are not met. Is call night a punishment? In addition, most full time work 6 days a week, including late call nights, and threat of a second night. Yet, the company boasts a wonderful work life balance, and even time made for volunteering with the community. There is NO time for any of this.

Bosses and colleagues don't often work together equally to meet goals and referrals. If one colleague's goals are met, that colleague makes no effort to assist other colleagues with their goals, even if the other colleague has made several referrals to help the original colleague with their goals. Those colleagues aren't in competition, but act if they are.

Company is slow to make changes. System is mainly archaic. Only recently, small parts of the system are coming up to date and look from this century. 

Many servicing functions for customers are becoming more and more back office. There is a main phone number to call, and no way for us to assist the caller besides calling for them, but the same process applies. I wish we could help the customer in the branch, instead of "call this number and sit on hold until the call center picks up for you, we aren't capable of helping you in the branch"

advice: There is more management than working unfortunately. I love my managers. They were good. I was lucky to have them as managers, yet other managers did not perform the few duties they had very well. I suggest that people be relocated out of management where appropriate. Time/experience  is not a good indication of a person's ability to lead.
pros:
- excellent people in IT
- good work life balance
- employee feedback is listened to
- downtown location
- great benefits
cons:
- very slow progress
- old strategies
- too much security (beyond reasonable)
- downtown location

summary: Stop and consider the impact on your resume to work here
pros: Large company with competitive benefits, has attracted great employees from many respected companies but it ends there
cons: Where do I start? Struggles to run efficiently and within US regulations. Great staff in the banks but home office senior management combats with Spain oversight that is not in tune with US ways and respect for employees or US regulations. This creates the kind of environment where "they eat their own young" is an apt description. Many workers that came from great companies but found no greatness become unhappy and paranoid. No respect for diversity or inclusion. No respect for life work balance.

advice: Continue to modernize the company, both on the customer side as well as the employee side. Invest in organizational structure changes.
pros: Highly professional environment that never loses its sense of humor and enjoyment. I loved the Cafeteria and Starbucks at the Columbia Park offices, along with the gym and other benefits that includes working at the bank.
cons: Most of the techologic processes are way behind. Software is out dated and the exchange of data and communication is terrible. These issues often caused a decrease in productivity.

advice:
Too many male mangers and too few female managers in Retail Branches - more balance is something needed.
Micromanagement in Retail Branches happens too often and has been exacerbated in times of Covid - trust your staff, they do a great job.
pros: Gives lots of trust and freedom to experiment. Opportunity to lead and work on projects that make a real positive impact on colleagues and customers.
cons: Lack of transparency during time of redundancies - sometimes it appears that close relationships and friendships (instead of competencies) are what will decide if you keep your job.

advice: There as been more dialogue between management and employees, there need to be more following up. Transition between department is extremely difficult. Create pathway for employees to immerse in different side of the business : ex sales to corporate etc...
pros: The company is finally facing it's shortcomings, upper management seems to be sharing the right message to move things forward.
cons: Technology is still below par, work life balance is not enforced by all branches of management. Communication is very poor specially with different branches of the business

summary: Gets in the way of itself
advice: Find the right people and keep them.  Develop a strong digital first strategy, and stick with it.  Build the bench strength below the director level with talented, digital natives that will see the organization as a place to truly develop their careers.
pros:
- Respected global institution
- Seasoned leadership at the Director, Sr. Director, and Executive Director levels
cons:
- Overly complicated in nearly everything it does
- Very hesitant and slow to do anything
- Frequent turnover leads to constant feeling of uncertainty
- Maintains a very branch-centric DNA
- Low collaboration globally

advice:
Speak the truth and stop hiding info from CEO
Stop been afraid of telling like it is.
Focus on the projects that are important for the business
pros: Opportunities to  improve the current process and fix all that's wrong with this place. Benefits are very good.
cons:
Most managers don't have real life experience and are totally clueless, they hide a lots of info from the CEO. 
HR is clueless
Claims of been fair but far from it.
Every project is an emergency, no planning, always fire fighting

summary: Personal banker and small business specialists
pros:
*The whole district works together. All of the branches are open to help others. 
*Good leadership 
*they want you to grow 
*they focus in service to the customer more than sales and that creates more revenue and loyal customers. 
*good 401K match and benefits
cons:
*If you come from a different institution probably they will pay you more than an internal that just got promoted. 
* in the branches and training facilities we waste too much paper just to keep records for operations purposes

advice: Listen to employees. But REALLY listen. Don't ask for positive coerced opinions. Assess the core jobs/daily tasks and work on improving them instead of improving everything around it. Family days and team building won't make the day-to-day more manageable.
pros: Relationships between coworkers is great and makes. Benefits are pretty good. The new president is looking for new ways to improve
cons: Too many old school managers how think that hard work means long hours sitting at your desk. NO PROFESIONAL GROWTH at all unless you have right connections. Your future here dependes solely on who you know or connection with, rather than hard work

summary: Good place to pad your resume while working a second job to get by
advice: Know that many people who work there are unhappy, not that anything will be done about it. The 40%+ turnover rate speaks volumes.
pros:
PTO and the ability to buy more PTO
Most of my co-workers, particularly the ones that like to go out drinking after work
If you have a laptop you can work from home from time to time
OT is offered in some positions
cons:
Like my title suggested, the bank does not pay a living wage. I worked there for 10 years and the only raises that I received was when I took a new position (twice).  The cash bonuses that you receive at the end of the year come to about $12 a week after taxes. The cost of living raises are.....not there. Most people that I worked with had to work a second job.

A lot of of posted positions that are higher grade levels state that Spanish speaking is a plus, but not required. While that may not sound like an issue, most of the time those positions are given to those that came over from Spain. So, if you want to move up, learn the language. No, they don't offer language lessons.

The tech is old, unstable and unusable. The customers of the bank deserve better than what is offered. Whatever Santander introduces, other banks have done it for years.

The benefits, medical-wise, fall short. The coverage for the one medical plan that's offered is minimal and the deductibles are high. The only other plan is a medical health savings account. Oh, and the deductions from your paycheck are high and that's WITHOUT a family plan. The dental and vision plans are pretty solid, though.

So like I said, work there for a few years, get some experience, get some references, get some pennies in your pocket and then look elsewhere.

advice: There's only so much lipstick you can put on a pig.....
pros:
-Close to "T"
-Meet some international people
-If you're really into the mainframe
-If you need to kill a year in between jobs and they offer you a very good rate, then maybe
cons:
-Very antiquated systems.  Windows 2003 was common, filling out tickets by scanning paper. Hard to get a password to even access a lot of systems.
-Very low professionalism:
  Managers undermining other managers
  Higher than usual nepotism and croneyism
  Very high turnover. McDonald's like in some areas.
  People yelling, carrying on, histrionics, etc.
-Columbia Park facility is old and crowded. Very hard to get a conference room.
-Poor promotions, lack of growth
-Onboarding takes a long, long time. Think-- just getting your laptop is a minor miracle

advice: Show leadership.  Told once that I could not have the difficult conversations if i were to become a manager.  If that's the case I would fit right into your management style, as you just had a lame duck CEO layoff 20% of the sales force.
pros: Other than the people you work closest with none
cons: At least my DE like the word business as usual...even with the pandemic. Poor work life balance and very little room for promotion. Management likes to make changes without thinking them through and without warning. I kept my job, but do their layoffs over the phone with out going CEO

advice: Better internal organisation so that there is consistency in the customer service that is delivered. Better promotional opportunities; one can never get past PBA level unless you are really desperate for someone.
pros: money feibility flexibility some branches are really nice to work in because of the staff which makes the day go a bit quicker. Other than that there isn't anything else to say.
cons: there are too many to list. It is a very badly organised company with a lot of backwards procedures that don't help the customers or the staff. Often it is embarrassing to work for Santander because of the poor quality customer service.

summary: You can learn a lot, but don't expect transparency and meritocracy to grow
advice:
I've seen a lot of moral harassment while in my unit at the HQ. Be sure to denounce it to the HR
A lot of takers among managers. Some managers don't want their team to grow. I'm glad I left the company and found other that value my effort.
pros:
Security
Big, global company
Exposition
Friendly culture - in general, willingness to help
cons:
A lot of vanity among sr management
Be sure to get the right manager
Not clear rules to divide bonus - lack of transparency
Lack of meritocracy - a lot of "I like you, so I will promote you"

advice: Hire capable district management team with a proven track record of management and not individual sales performance. Promote from within. Many capable team members leaving because if this. Lead by example. Go out on sales calls / onsites with team members for coaching and support opportunities. Follow marketing trends. No one goes goes to the bank anymore.  With technology today why would they. Focus on technology to generate sales. Especially in the business segment.
pros: Salary, friendly colleagues, great work experience to move forward in a career in financial services, great incentives
cons: Disorganization at senior/district level, poor guidance, very critical. No work life balance since forced to make calls after bank hours if credit card goals aren't made.  Not a job for students. Too stressful. Management does not lead by example. Micromanagement is an understatement.

advice: Select real professionals and people with the knowledge and commitment to improve the bank
pros: Supposedly a good salary. Maybe the possibility of moving laterally
cons: Horrible organizational culture. Higher ups and director are the ones getting the bonuses and at the same time making mistakes that cost the bank millions and millions. There is no accountability. When a project fails everybody blames everybody. There are managers who dont have any idea about how to manage the day to day operations. Goals at all levels and for all products are un-achievable.

summary: Not a good place for ethical and honest people
advice: Listen to the people that do the work. Your upper management is out of touch and unaware. Morale is terrible.
pros: Many good individuals in support and middle management. Lots of good ideas at grass roots level. Pay used to be good. New hires don't get great pay.
cons: Horrible executive and C-level management  Board must be asleep. Laying off IT staff was a big mistake. Cuts only affect workers not upper management.

advice:
the way you are  managing I would say you really push your people to leave company to down size in many position. need to be honest with your guys , play fair .
HR need to have more recognition about  people
pros: Diverse people, respectable guys, talented and hard working, even with lots of pressure they have from higher levels
cons:
Worse management , new CIO try to put pressure on people of IT department
load unfair them since their financial status is not doing good keep pressure on department to shows good figures on their performance.
no promotion any more, HR playing with eligible guys to do not give promotion.
no respect to IT guys from C levels.  I would say Janitor has more retrospection than ITS , VP's always demanding bad attitude with their IT guys.

advice:
1. Employees know when leaders don't walk the "Respect" "Personal" "Fair" 
"Simple" talk and eventually customers figure it out too.   2. Being not-as-bad-as-BOA-and-Wells and hiring their execs isn't a business strategy.   3. Build your mortgage strategy for the 21st century, not the 20th.
pros: Good health insurance, flexible time off, environment not as bad as some other large banks.  Retail does "Personal" well with customers, who generally like the bank.
cons: Have worked in financial services for a long time and never seen such mediocre management.   Generally true for retail, especially bad in mortgage, where Operations has a distinct culture of disrespect and making-things-more-difficult-for the straight-commissioned originators and other customer-facers; the worst offenders have been rewarded.   Multiple levels of sales management whose skills are limited to holding meetings and "rah rah, go work/sell more."   Employee surveys are given only lip service.   Have experienced subtle discrimination.

advice: Just keep communication open with the advisors, yes we have chats but some people are sometimes afraid to feel stupid to reach out. Its sometimes nice to be asked how we are doing even if we aren't having issues.
pros: Training was thorough and very helpful. I like being able to take calls and assist customers with issues that they may be having with their accts or even just giving them answers to simple problems. Softlanding, has wonderful coaches who are knowledgeable and helpful to us trainees
cons: Some of the calls are rough and when some of us get unsure it isn't always easy to reach out through a message when you have someone yelling at you on the phone line. I have experienced some customers who are rude and are bullies and its a shame that some can do a survey on us but we can't do a survey on them haha.

summary: Old school bank mentality with old school bank politics.
advice: When you send out internal company surveys to solicit our evaluations and feedback, listen.  Don't penalize loyalty.  Typical salary increases are very minimal year over year and only way to truly increase pay is to quit and get re-hired from outside the bank.
pros: Stability.  Santander does a good job at minimizing layoffs and if a department has a downsize, they will try to fit you into another compatible area of the bank.
cons: Below industry standard pay.  Very minimal raises.  One percent raise across the board for everyone does not keep up with inflation.  Very hard to move up within the ranks.  Lack of empowerment.  Non-existent company culture.  Unfortunately the company only gives lip service to listening to their own employees ideas and would rather pay outside consultants to give feedback instead of getting it from their own people.

pros: Great company to grow and advance within. Very close to other employees of the bank which gives opportunity to get to know partners of the bank and management very well. They want to help you learn and grow and they start from your first day.
cons: As far as the technology part go this bank it needs a lot of updating. Some procedures are ancient compared to other big time banks like chase. Systems are dated but with time and integration they are updating.

summary: A great employer for talented individuals.
advice: Continue on this path of transformation and this organization will achieve a great success in the future.
pros: Great company to work for. New leadership provides a breath of fresh air. Very competitive benefits.
cons: Busy but rewarding environment. Santander is not perfect, but provides a great platform for its employees to make a positive change. Management has been rapidly transforming this organization into a world class institution, but there is still more work to be done.

advice: Do not tell employees that they can't get an exceptional rating unless they are a unicorn. Unicorns do not exist which implies that the exceptional rating is an impossible goal only put there for looks. So if that I the case, change the grading system as it is apparently rigged.
pros: The entry pay rate was good at that time and they had cool amenities like food trucks, dress down, paid volunteer time, prayer room, massage appointments, carnival events, and the like.
cons: All that said, recent raises of minimum wages means you could work at a fast food place and get paid the same or better. Last I heard, they are no longer using their NRH location due to moving everyone to remote work which means no amenities. Before all of these changes, I noticed people only moved up if you knew somebody otherwise it didn't matter if you had the skills.

advice: Be kind, be patient, be fair and objective. Establish a career path for people to follow and promote on those attributes.
pros: Globally the company is doing well which provides job security for now and in the future
cons: Because the companies main headquarters are internnational, so is their top of the chain leadership team.  I'm past 4 years here in the US there has been complete turnover, not once, not twice, three times.  This is bad news because each new leader completely changes the behaviors, priorities, activities, sales plan for the whole company.  They are not patient with change and most recently have transitioned into a culture of fear that is used motivate and force change fast.

advice: More transparency and communication.
pros:
Even though I have a questionable background - I had a rap sheet when I was a teenager, the bank was very supportive and my managers let me stay and work anyway. What an awesome place! If you're worried about not getting hired because you have a record, have ppr credit, this is the place to be. I'm just very thankful.  Too good to be true? Obviously it's on case by case basis - but have a look at this recent article and you'll see.
 Google Ritu Singh  and New York Post
cons: Promotion and performance process systematically restricts your growth - managers will submit you a 4 rating if they want to give you a 3 because it always gets knocked down by the "committee".

advice: Grow up and be more professional
pros: Some manager are cool and not floor gossipers, the benefits was cool and the pay was alright it paid the bills.
cons: They first train you for a department that you are not going to and have absolutely nothing to do with the department you are going to. The job description did not have collections and once I started working about 8 months in it turned into collecting from old past due accounts. You don’t get a bonus monthly for collecting.

summary: Lots of potential due to size, but greatly disappointing.  No cohesive vision of where they want to be.
advice: Figure out what you want to be good at and stick with that.  Don't go into areas of the market half-heartedly.  Fully commit, or don't commit at all.
pros: somewhat collegial atmosphere, relaxed environment
cons: low-caliber of long-term staff, no clear or cohesive vision of a strategic plan.  Unsure where they should be positioned in terms of traded markets, thus no real commitment in many areas.

summary: Always changing. Never a solid direction
advice: Have better systems in place. Online banking has tons of issues and can be very user unfriendly. NCR has admitted that we aren't a priority which is terrible. If you want your branches to be the best, you need to pull your own weight. Make sure your branches are ready to rollout new systems effectively. And for the love of God don't let a data breach go unheard of for 3 months.
pros: It's a job. Potential to make more money. Good if you live in a busy area. Looks good on a resume.
cons: Staff is always changing. Bank doesn't know what it wants to do. Super indecisive as a company. Incentive plan is ridiculous. No way you're getting any bonus worth the work. Also.... There was a recent data breach with all employee information leaking out including SSN and compensation. Something is up. Beware

advice: Consider internal talent prior to hiring externally.  Take the time to identify competent executive leadership, select a strategic approach and commit without material change to the plan.  Improve and increase communication to employees.  Provide clear direction on career path.
pros: Initially the people were a positive.  However given the number of resource changes and the new engagement model, there are no pros to working for this organization.
cons: The number is concerns are plentiful.  There are too many organizational changes including several CEOs in an short period of time.  The consistent flow of new executive leadership impacts moral, creates further instability and limits growth and progress towards improvements.  The location is a challenge and the organization does not promote work life balance.  Please do not consider working for this company, they do not value their employees.

summary: Working at Santander will ruin your career
advice: This comment is directed to Santander in Madrid - Sell the company and get out of the US.
pros: The 401(k) contributions made by the employee the contribution made by the company vests immediately
cons: Executive management at Santander changes almost annually, which results in corresponding turnover at the levels beneath. If you are terminated as part of these annual changes in Executive management, no severance whatsoever will be provided. The people who stay at Santander spend their time covering up the company's many shortcomings, not fixing the sources of the shortcomings. Management does not want to hear any "bad" news - especially if it's true.

advice: Change the corporate culture.  There needs to be more training for management and people should be held accountable for the training received.
pros: The pay was good and I worked with some great people.  New headquarters in Dallas is top notch and not an expense spared.  Desks, computers, and break rooms are awesome.
cons: It's a very negative work environment that does not encourage communication.  I worked there for 1.5 years and after a year I knew it was not for me.  The work environment is great but the people are not trained or encouraged to use standard corporate protocale or basic communication skills.  It was a constant challenge to deal with the lack of morale and bad culture.  Bottom line, the corporate CULTURE IS BAD

advice: At least pretend you care about team members rather then making it very obvious you don't.
pros: Pay is competitive and they have good products for the customers, including checking and credit cards. Convenient ATMs in many CVS stores.  There is not much more I can say in the pro column.
cons: Unrealistic expectations and low employee moral. Company is in a cost saving mode, laying off many non branch job families. They have no customer service commitment nor team member commitment.

advice: Title is not that important.  At the end of the day, it is the money people is using to judge the worthy of their job.  Downplay on the pay is not a very smart move.  Sooner or later people will find better opportunity and leave.  It would be too late by then.
pros: Environment is dynamic.  There are plenty of opportunities to advance your technical skills.  State of the art IT infrastructure.  Good place to horn your skill set.
cons: Pay is bias.  The rewarding system is broken.  High performer doesn't mean you get the high pay.  Management sees the problem but has no intention to fix it so that the good, knowledgeable employees would stay.  The employee turnaround rate is high.  10 days vacation is not very competitive.

advice: The direction is the right one. Keep going. It is not by chance that the company had so far a terrific history of 160 years of success.
pros: A strong culture that is improving every day. A purpose that is unique in the financial industry. A level of ethic that is as high as it is in the most ethical companies.
cons: Formalism, hierarchy and somehow a global mindset that still needs to be improved. Also, too much committees to take decisions.

summary: Pay is good but you will be incredibly stressed out
advice: Seriously consider investing in new software. The reason why this Bank is constantly failing the stress test is because your processes and systems leave room for bankers and tellers to make so many errors.
pros: The bonus compensation is better than most banks. That is literally the only good thing I can say.
cons: You will work for every single penny. The sales pressure isn't as high as other companies but the systems and processes will make your life miserable. While other banks are actually going paperless and making it easier to perform maintenance and other transactions, Santander is going the opposite direction. Everything takes so long to execute and you need so many documents just to complete one task. The pay is decent but there is a reason why people don't even last a year in this company. Update your software!

summary: Not the best experience for the banking business
advice: So far it is pretty notorious there is a strong need to hire more people, it makes no sense for such a huge company to ask their employees to work extra hours every day
pros: I have to admit that they have a great human resources department, always looking forward to solving any problems the employee might come across
cons:
Lots of extra hours
No benefits for employees 
Incredibly strict punctuality (every late arrival has to be accounted for)
Anty union policies

summary: Guaranteed to make you quit in under 90 days
advice: Be involved in your branches more. I left because this was the worst place I’ve ever worked. There was no communication with management. It was disgusting how people treated one another as well. Coming from outside banking, it made me hate the industry I tried so hard to get into.
pros:
Easy Interview Process
Paid Training 

There isn’t really a lot of good to say about Santander from the level I was at...
cons:
Disconnect between branches and management 
Sunday’s with no time and a half in some branches
Favoritism outweighs balance
No work/life balance 
Far, outdated tech.
No personal leave
Cannot use PTO before you acrue it even if they give it to you in January.

advice: I say sell this bank and close the door.
pros: Talented and amazing people that bust their butt (unfortunately, do not get recognized enough)
cons:
AWFUL systems with teams that can't support them.
IT runs the bank (with their poor systems and practices)
Does not promote a risk minded culture. 
Poor leadership and management.
Unethical practices.
Weak recruiting process and placement. People in roles that clearly aren't qualified.
Micromanagers.
No dress code.
Bullying.
Nothing gets done. There's a clash between the ones that want to do the right thing and people that don't-- seems like some people are part of a mafia and there are cover ups with issues and problems. How can you fix anything without understanding the root cause and holding certain teams/ people accountable? 
Lack of accountability

advice: Instead of trying to be just like all the other big banks, provide something different like well compensated, well trained, experienced staff members.
pros: Well advertised, great lending and banking rates, exceptional bonus potential (previously).
cons: Constant turnover at upper management, company focus changed regularly.  Most recent CEO  sought to make all reps interchangeable and failed to recognize the importance of individual relationships.  Approach was to make every customer interaction a cookie cutter transaction aimed at collecting information and providing a sales solution.  Did not value educated, professional employees and the impact they can have on long term sustained banking relationships.

summary: For a bank that preaches respect, they sure don’t give it to you unless you are a select banker.
advice: Don’t have a select banker and relationship banker in the same branch... keep only one banker per branch licensed, and provide more incentive for relationship bankers to actually refer to the select banker instead of keeping it for themselves (because nobody wants to miss out on a 2000 revenue credit SIS sale for a 500 revenue credit select referral, especially when their work was what uncovered the need in the first place). Whether you do that, or something different, something has to be done to bridge the gap between select bankers and relationship bankers, and either make the working relationship easier or start keeping only one licensed banker per branch.
pros:
Great place to get yourself licensed. They used Kaplan which I found to be very helpful in their test prep to get you licensed.
During licensing, you dedicate all of your time to licensing.
Great place to build up work experience.
Company culture overall is not bad, however they do not seem to live it so much as speak it, especially when it comes to respect (unless you are a select banker).
cons:
Select bankers can do whatever they want, and you will be forced to pick up the slack as well as refer high net worth clients. Basically, your hard work is getting them paid. 
Because of the select program, it makes it a bit harder to develop yourself when you are in a select branch, due to many high network clients being referrals you are expected to give to the select banker.
Make sure to get any employment promises in writing!! They will promise you bonuses that do not actually exist, at least that was what my recruiter did, and completely denied that she said what she did.
You are not respected if you are not a select banker, you will be expected to do all the maintenance, while referring any big business to the select banker, but you are still supposed to meet unrealistic goals (without access to high net worth clients).

summary: It is who you know not what you know
advice: They need better Human Resource Team and advocate.They could do a better job at really investigating insidences of Abuse of Power. The Managers speak poorly to the workers. It's a my way or the highway culture.They have not done enough for working mom's and Covid 19 pandemic. Not a very inclusive environment.lots of cliques.
pros: Medical Benefits and since Covid realistic hours 9-4
cons: They do not promote Good People. Tend to keep employees on who don't have the skills which is great for that employee but for the other hardworking ones it is disappointing.

advice: Continue to lean on employee networks as a voice for employees.
pros:
Great onboarding experience, especially for a pandemic. Had all my equipment and instructions delivered to my house and had all the meetings I needed to have to get me started quickly to do my job.
Good access to tools and resources. Santander is also improving vision for company and for employees through employee networks.
cons: Family planning/ adoption / infertility benefits could improve, especially for LGBT+. community. Recently improved leave policy, but it seems that Santander lags competitors in this space.

advice: Keep your minds open. Continue to support your employees and listen to them. Your employees do value the work you have done making Santander a great place to work. Thank you!
pros: The marketing/communications team is wonderful! The people are great and benefits are excellent. The company promotes a healthy work life balance and takes employee satisfaction seriously.
cons: The marketing division is growing and is experiencing growing pains. Processes need a bit of finesse however this is to be expected with a company on the rise and finding its voice  in the global business world.

advice: Look at your competitor's technology and service commitments to their clients.  Start living by your slogan (Simple, Personal, Fair) instead of just slapping it on emails.  Also, conference calls aren't the answer to everything.
pros: Decent benefits and 401k match, relative autonomy (in my role anyway)
cons: Outdated technology, no accountability with back office,  bureaucratic procedures makes it extremely difficult for front end sales staff to manage client relationships and  close business.  Unclear master plan in the US.  Extremely high turnover (even by retail standards), no consistency in service.  Retail branches are extremely understaffed.

advice: N/A
pros: I am thrilled to be continuing my career with such an amazing team at Santander Bank. Everyone is super nice; management shows a genuine interest in making sure people are happy and have a chance to succeed in their role. Change can be scary but I am pleased with my decision to switch to Santander and I would do it again. My role is 100% remote and I have had no trouble with onboarding and very limited technical issues.
cons: Santander's underwriting packages can be a bit too long. Redundancy can be limited.

summary: I have experienced a diversified role in the banking industry.
advice: I believe Management is going through many changes and doing their best with all the new acquisitions for the company and its employees.
pros: I have been with the company for three years.  One year was an acqusition of several companies and experiencing the changes that take place.  I have acquired several new experiences during my tenure, mainly customer service and how vital that is for the company.
cons: The job description did not entail the type of repition of your job.  I feel I have more to offer a company.

advice: Just keep listening to what the front liners are telling. This will benefit the company in the long run if you take notes from the direct contacts with clients.
pros: Good benefits and good colleagues to work with. Senior management is always willing to listen.
cons: Growing pains as the other reviewer has said. Customer care call center can be painful to deal with. You may have to watch out the work life balance. may become hectic and really stressful if you are not careful due to what is expected of you!

pros: Good colleagues and team spirit made working there very pleasurable. As a customer service rep. it was nice to deal with lots of different clients (both businesses and individuals). You get a lot of support from colleagues.
cons:
Not enough people to handle peak periods, which can lead to a lot of lag in service times later on which in turns frustrated customers.

All open positions were sometimes not accessible, which led to some frustrations when I discovered that there would have been an interesting position but it was already filled.

summary: Great place not a great team
advice: Training is a big thing. PMO direction needs to be taken seriously and the band-aid pulled off in regards to making a change or not.
pros: The people overall are fantastic to work with. So.even of the best I've met. Definitely a work hard play hard place.
cons: Manager was great as an individual  contributor, but sub pat as a manager. Playing hard was reserved for those on the inside of certain cliques, as with most jobs. Some folks were not counseled on poor performance or attitude for one reason or another.

pros: Challenging work, great people, awesome downtown dallas location, you have very smart people that know the industry, young eager company making its name in the finance industry, They live their core values
cons: pay can be a little better, benefits still need improvement, slow periods followed by extremely busy time with overtime work.

advice: sometimes it gets difficult to innovate, eliminate barriers and move forward in the career because of rigid structures and heavy load of bureaucracy. i believe the retail banking also lags its peers in efficiency and customer relations
pros: good benefits such as extended maternity leave, health insurance, transportation, etc. many areas are available and mobility is encouraged and possible, not only between areas but also countries
cons: lower than average salaries comparing with global bank peers due to generous benefits, heavy bureaucracy and a classic spanish structure with quite rigid hierarchy.

advice: Be more organized and find ways to include the interns more in their overall work.
pros: I really enjoyed the corporate culture there, people were very friendly and management seemed very intelligent. They had a good, structured overall intern program and strived to make us feel very welcome.
cons: My particular department was not very structured regarding having work for me to do on a daily basis and a lot of it was self-learning as opposed to hands-on training. Sometimes I felt a little babied as an intern as well with the way management treated us too.

summary: RUN, Do Not Walk Away from Santander!
advice:
Santander globally is an organization of which to be proud.  Santander in the U.S. is an organization of which to be embarrassed.  Either get serious about turning things around, invest in the technology required to upgrade the bank, understand that branch banking is dying faster than you can build unneeded new branches, and once and for all, get SERIOUS about the talent you need to attract in order to succeed.  Upgrade your risk management practices and people, go after the executive talent who can turn Santander U.S. around (hint:  your most recent CEO and his "team" are NOT the answer!!) and open your purse and PAY PEOPLE WHAT THEY ARE WORTH!!  

If you won't do that?  Then just end the pain.  Sell the bank for what you can get and get the heck out of the U.S.
pros: Other than the fact that you would receive a paycheck, I cannot think of a positive reason to work at Santander.
cons:
The culture is poisonous.  That's not an overstatement, it is simply a poisonous place to work.  40 hour weeks feel like 90.  Employee morale is at a level too low to describe -- I've not seen anything like it in my career.  Everyone I know is actively looking to leave Santander, and employees openly and brazenly discuss at work their job search efforts and status.  I even know two successful mid-career people who simply resigned without a new position lined up because they could not take the environment anymore.  HR is the most negative and least responsive of anywhere I've worked in my entire 30-year career.  Annual reviews are useless, as HR tells every manager how many of each rating level he is permitted to have on his team.  So no matter how good a job your employees have done, you are not permitted to provide them with a rating (or a raise - they're non-existent) commensurate with their performance.  You are forced to rate them at the level HR tells you they should be.  This HR practice, called stacked ranking, was debunked and abandoned by reputable companies a decade or more ago.  At Santander?  It's relatively new and an example of the progressive HR policies in which they take pride.  

There is little if any decision making authority in the U.S. -- anything of substance has to be decided in Spain, and the process of getting a decision made is excruciatingly slow and painful.  The U.S. executives put in place to run the company are fired and replaced on a continual basis, and the bank has reached the point where it can only attract executive talent from the bottom level of who is available -- the people with the skills and talent needed to turn this bank around simply and wisely will not come work here.  Additionally, the most senior positions have been used as 2 - 3 year vacations for an endless series of Spanish executives who know little or nothing about banking in the U.S. and do little or nothing of substance while they are here.  In the five years that I have worked at Santander, we have had 5 CEO's, 4 Chief Credit Officers and I, a mid-level manager, have had 7 bosses.
